newsitem.title: PERU: Peruvian police say ready for last-resort assault.
newsitem.headline: Peruvian police say ready for last-resort assault.

text.p: A crack 200-strong Peruvian police force has completed training around a model of the besieged Japanese ambassador's residence and is ready in case an assault is ordered against Marxist guerrillas inside, police sources said on Monday.
"We are waiting for orders from the government. We are prepared," said a high-level police source, who asked not to be named.
Although the Peruvian government has said repeatedly it wants to negotiate a peaceful solution, it has not ruled out the use of force to end the 13-day-old crisis.
The police sources said they estimated an operation to free the 83 VIP hostages from their roughly 20 captors would take between three and five minutes.
Security experts from around the world have arrived in Lima in recent days to advise the Peruvian government on possible military action against the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement rebels.
